ca_corner_boulder_2.blurb: Corner Boulder is a single boulder in the Happy Boulders zone of the Volcanic Tablelands, near Bishop in the Eastern Sierra, at roughly 4,500 feet. It sits a short way uphill and east of Slow Dance Cave, among a cluster of large dark blocks. There are nine problems, all of them on the easier end: mostly V0 and V1, with one at V2 and one below V0. The west face carries most of the climbing, including a pair of highballs next to each other, so pad coverage and spotters matter on the taller lines. It suits climbers warming up or looking for moderate problems before heading to the harder caves nearby.

ca_candy_land.blurb: Candy Land is a sport crag in Bowman Valley, one of the clusters of bolted climbing below Bowman Lake Dam in the Lake Tahoe region, at around 5,500 feet. The wall is a set of big slabs broken by a small arching roof, set between two neighbouring crags. It has nine bolted routes, with a spread from 5.6 up to 5.11: three of the easiest grade, a few in the 5.8 to 5.9 range, a pair at 5.10, and one 5.11. A couple of the routes run two pitches, so the climbing is not all single-pitch. Good for a mixed group with moderate and harder leaders.

ca_l_slab_lakeview_slab.blurb: L-Slab/Lakeview Slab is a granite slab on a rocky hillside within Lake Perris State Recreation Area in the Inland Empire, a short distance from the better-known Big Rock. It stands roughly 500 feet above the San Jacinto Valley. The faces are well featured. There are nine routes in all, mostly trad-rated lines that also carry bolts, plus one sport route. Grades run from 5.7 through 5.11, with three at 5.8 and a few at 5.11, so it works for moderate leaders and for stronger climbers looking for something harder.

ca_leaning_towers.blurb: Leaning Towers is a small sport crag on Fairview Mountain in the High Desert near Apple Valley, in the Land of the Lost section at around 3,900 feet. The main feature is a tower that visibly tilts, a few hundred feet from Reed's Pinnacle. Eight of the nine routes are bolted and one is a trad crack. Most of the sport lines sit in the 5.10 range, with one 5.11, plus an easy 5.7 sport line and the 5.7 crack as the entry points. With only nine routes it is a stop within a bigger day on Fairview Mountain.

ca_lenticular_dome.blurb: Lenticular Dome is a dome in the Wonderland Valley section of Joshua Tree National Park, at about 4,400 feet. This part of the valley draws more climbers than the eastern half. It has nine routes, mostly trad, with one bolted line and one top-rope. Grades start around 5.5 and top out near 5.10, with four routes at 5.9 and a couple at 5.7, so it leans toward moderate climbing. A couple of lines are two pitches long. The walk in from the valley takes a good chunk of an hour, which keeps it a half-day or longer outing.

_expect.name: Mm! Mm! Good! (aka Campbell Soup) Boulder

ca_mm_mm_good_aka_campbell_soup_boulder.blurb: This is a single mid-sized boulder near Cisco Grove, in the Donner/Truckee part of the I-80 corridor near Lake Tahoe, at about 7,200 feet. It is one of the two boulders in the Nearly Clear Cut group, and the only one with problems, and it sits right next to the lot, so the walk is only a few steps. There are nine problems, from VB up to V5: a cluster of V1s, a few easy lines, a single V2 and V3, and two at V5. One easy problem follows a crack. Good for a short session with a mix of beginner and harder problems.

ca_3_upper_right.blurb: Upper - Right is the highest section of School Rock on Donner Summit along the I-80 corridor near Lake Tahoe, at roughly 7,200 feet. It consists of several tiers of rock stacked above the main right-hand cliff of the formation. There are nine routes, mostly trad plus two sport lines, running from 5.8 to 5.11. The spread is one 5.8, two 5.9s, three 5.10s and three 5.11s, so it suits climbers stepping up from moderate crack climbing as well as stronger leaders. The trail up can fade in places, so the first visit may take a little route-finding.
